simple.meaning: פַּלָּצוּת (pallâtsûwth) is a Hebrew word meaning “affright.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פַּלָּצוּת (H6427) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 21:6, with occurrences in Job, Psalms, Isaiah, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פַּלָּצוּת (H6427) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פַּלָּצוּת (H6427) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פַּלָּצוּת (pallâtsûwth) / H6427 is traced through Job 21:6, Psalms 55:6, Isaiah 21:4, Ezekiel 7:18 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: When I remember, I am troubled.

timeline.evidenceText: When I remember, I am troubled.
I said, “Oh that I had wings like a dove!
My heart flutters. Horror has frightened me. The twilight that I desired has been turned into trembling for me.
They will also clothe themselves with sackcloth, and horror will cover them. Shame will be on all faces, and baldness on all their heads.
